name: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
localName: Tajine de poulet aux citrons confits et olives
summary: Chicken braised with saffron, ginger, onion, preserved lemon and green olives into a silky, tangy golden sauce.
story: Chicken with preserved lemon and olives is among the best-known Moroccan tagines, named for the conical clay pot it is cooked in. It is a typical family lunch and also appears at gatherings, with bread to mop up the sauce. The braise relies on a lot of onion and gentle heat.

items.name: Preserved lemons
items.note: pulp discarded, rind rinsed and sliced

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry. Toss with the ginger, turmeric, pepper, salt and half of the garlic and let stand for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot or tagine base over medium-low heat. Cook the onions for 8 to 10 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken, the remaining garlic, cinnamon and the saffron with its soaking water. Turn the chicken a few times for 5 minutes until the pieces are lightly golden and coated.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Pour in the water or stock so it comes halfway up the chicken. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook on low for 35 minutes, turning the pieces once.

steps.title: Add lemon and olives
steps.text: Add the preserved lemon rind and olives and simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes. The chicken should be very tender and the sauce should reduce to a thick glossy gravy.

steps.title: Finish with herbs
steps.text: Stir in half the coriander and parsley and cook 2 minutes. Taste; the preserved lemon and olives add salt, so add more only if needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a serving dish, spoon the sauce over, and scatter with the remaining herbs. Serve with crusty bread or couscous.

tips: Grate the onions: they melt into the sauce and give it body without needing flour.
Rinse the preserved lemon and olives to avoid an over-salty sauce.
Cook on low heat; a hard boil makes the chicken stringy and the sauce split.
Use only the lemon rind; the pulp is very salty and bitter.

swaps.swap: Use the zest of 1 fresh lemon and 2 tbsp lemon juice added at the end, plus an extra pinch of salt; less complex but still bright.
Use extra turmeric (1/2 tsp more) for colour; the aroma will differ.
A heavy casserole with a tight lid works well.
